modules.name: ridu
modules.summary: The ergonomic application facade for config, startup, and access decisions.

symbols.name: New
symbols.summary: Create an application from config and a document store.
symbols.signature: func New(applicationConfig Config, backend store.Store) (*App, error)
details: When compiled by ridu build, the application carries the exact ordered migration-history fingerprint used by official adapter readiness. Application-owned servers remain responsible for running readiness before admitting traffic.

symbols.name: Resolve
symbols.summary: Resolve executable config into a deterministic schema manifest.
details: Resolution runs plugin transforms without opening a database.

symbols.name: Execute
symbols.summary: Run the API, admin, jobs, and shutdown lifecycle.

parameters.name: applicationConfig
parameters.description: Executable collections, globals, plugins, tasks, and application policy.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Runtime infrastructure and framework-owned server settings.

returns.description: The first joined project-command, startup, serving, drain, or cleanup failure.

details: With project-command arguments, Execute resolves config and runs the versioned CLI protocol without applying runtime options or opening adapters. With no arguments, it starts the framework-owned HTTP server and requires WithStore.

Server startup opens the document store, opens optional upload storage, constructs the application, verifies readiness, binds the listener, and only then starts background workers. SIGINT or SIGTERM marks readiness as draining, shuts down HTTP work, drains workers, and closes lifecycle-owned adapters.
Execute blocks until the command or server lifecycle finishes. Return its error from main or log it as a fatal startup/runtime failure.

symbols.name: LocalizationConfig
symbols.summary: Content locales, fallback behavior, and optional request-scoped admin availability.

parameters.name: DefaultLocale
parameters.description: Locale selected when a request does not specify one.

parameters.name: DisableFallback
parameters.description: Requires exact locale values instead of following fallback chains.

parameters.name: AvailableLocales
parameters.description: Optionally reduces locales visible to one admin request without weakening API validation or authorization.

details: Leave Locales empty to disable content localization. When localization is enabled, DefaultLocale must name one configured locale and every fallback must also be configured.

FallbackLocales are checked in order after the requested locale unless DisableFallback is true. AvailableLocales only narrows the locale picker for the current admin request; it cannot add locales, change API validation, or grant access, and executable callbacks are never serialized into the schema manifest.
Assign this value to Config.Localization. Because the root package aliases the canonical core contract, an AvailableLocales callback names its input as core.LocaleAvailabilityContext.

symbols.name: WithStore
symbols.summary: Provide the singular document-store adapter through the Execute lifecycle.

parameters.name: factory
parameters.description: A lazy constructor invoked once when Execute starts the HTTP server.

returns.description: An option to pass directly to ridu.Execute.

details: WithStore is required only for the no-argument server branch of Execute. Project commands such as generate and check resolve config without applying this option, so they do not need DATABASE_URL or a reachable database.
The factory receives the server lifecycle context. Return an unopened error rather than terminating the process inside the factory; Execute wraps it as open document store and returns it to main.

The returned store must implement the base store.Store contract and every optional capability enabled by the application. Production startup also requires store.ReadinessStore unless ServerOptions.AllowUnverifiableReadiness delegates readiness checking to an external system.

Execute owns the returned adapter. On startup failure or shutdown it calls Close() or Close() error when implemented, bounded by ServerOptions.ShutdownTimeout. Optional upload storage closes first, then the document store.

symbols.name: WithProjectMigrations
symbols.summary: Register the selected adapter’s compiled migration driver for project commands.

parameters.name: driver
parameters.description: Compiled callback registry and adapter-owned project migration runner.

returns.description: An option to pass directly to ridu.Execute.

details: The driver is used only by project migration commands whose artifacts contain compiled data callbacks. It is not used by schema generation or the ordinary HTTP runtime.
symbols.example: ridu.WithProjectMigrations(sqlite.ProjectMigrations(transforms...))

symbols.name: WithAddress
symbols.summary: Configure the HTTP listen address independently from the store adapter.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: A Go net.Listen TCP address such as :8080 or 127.0.0.1:8080.

returns.description: An option to pass directly to ridu.Execute.

details: The default is :8080, which listens on every interface. Use a loopback address when Ridu must be reachable only through a local reverse proxy or during development.
This controls only the listener. Public host validation belongs to HandlerOptions.AllowedHosts.
symbols.example: ridu.WithAddress("127.0.0.1:8080")

symbols.name: WithUploadStorage
symbols.summary: Provide object storage through the Execute lifecycle.

parameters.name: factory
parameters.description: A lazy object-storage constructor invoked during server startup.

returns.description: An option to pass directly to ridu.Execute.

details: The factory runs only in the server branch. It supplies Config.Storage before application construction, keeping credentials and network setup out of the resolved schema manifest.
Upload-enabled config still needs a stable Config.StorageNamespace and a document store with the upload capability contracts. Closable object storage shuts down before the document store.

symbols.name: WithHandlerOptions
symbols.summary: Configure the generated HTTP handler used by Execute.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: HTTP security, limits, admin assets, observers, readiness, and worker settings.

returns.description: An option to pass directly to ridu.Execute.

details: Generated projects use this option to attach the compiled admin assets and environment-derived HTTP policy. Passing it replaces the complete HandlerOptions value; combine settings in one value rather than scattering repeated WithHandlerOptions calls.

symbols.name: WithServerOptions
symbols.summary: Configure production socket and graceful-drain bounds.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Socket, readiness admission, shutdown, and worker-drain settings.

returns.description: An option to pass directly to ridu.Execute.

details: Zero values select bounded production defaults. Repeating WithServerOptions replaces the complete value, so configure related bounds together.

symbols.signature: func NewTask[Input, Output any](slug string, handler TaskHandler[Input, Output], options ...TaskOption) TypedTask[Input, Output]
details: Add the returned definition to Config.Tasks. Input and output use strict JSON contracts, are capped by MaxTaskPayloadBytes, and never select executable code from serialized data. The backing store must implement store.TaskStore.

parameters.name: Result
parameters.description: Loads and decodes typed task status and output.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: Prevents queued work and fences a running attempt.

details: Only NewTask constructs a valid definition. Add it to Config.Tasks before using its runtime methods.
The handle slug/type contract must match the definition registered in the running application. HasOutput distinguishes a valid zero/null output from incomplete work.

symbols.name: TaskTimeout

symbols.name: RetryTask
symbols.summary: Return a retryable handler failure using configured backoff.
symbols.signature: func RetryTask(code string, cause error) error

symbols.name: RetryTaskAfter

symbols.name: AbortTask

symbols.signature: func AbortTask(code string, cause error) error
details: Use stable non-secret codes. Local runtime, store, and codec boundary failures use structured TaskError values. Handler panics and handler/output failures are classified into durable retry or dead-letter state instead.

symbols.name: Store
symbols.summary: Starts atomic transactions for operations.
details: All operation-engine reads and mutations, including read-only operations, run through a transaction.

symbols.name: Transaction
symbols.summary: Atomic document reads and mutations.

parameters.name: ApplyReferenceDelete
parameters.description:
ApplyReferenceDelete atomically plans incoming current-document
references, rejects when any restrict policy matches, and otherwise
nullifies/removes those values. Version snapshots remain immutable.

parameters.name: DeleteDocumentState
parameters.description:
DeleteDocumentState idempotently removes framework-owned database state
where the document is either the target or the owning principal.

parameters.description: Authorization predicate applied atomically with Filter.

parameters.name: IndexWindow

parameters.name: PopulationBudget
parameters.description:
PopulationBudget is shared by every recursive population read that
contributes to one response. Official adapters initialize a default when
callers omit it so direct store use cannot bypass the materialization cap.

parameters.name: PublishedOnly
parameters.description: Restrict versioned reads to published documents.

parameters.name: Locales
parameters.description:
Locales is the complete configured locale order used to decode canonical
localized storage. LocaleChain starts with the requested locale and then
contains effective fallbacks used by atomic filtering and sorting.

parameters.name: LocaleChain

symbols.name: AuthStore
symbols.summary: Persistence required by auth-enabled collections.

parameters.name: SetPasswordHash
parameters.description:
SetPasswordHash replaces a user-controlled password and atomically revokes
every session and API key for that user.

parameters.name: ChangePasswordHash
parameters.description:
ChangePasswordHash replaces a password only while its exact stored hash is
the hash verified by the caller. A successful change revokes every session
and API key. Exact hash comparison also fences hard-delete/same-ID
credential recreation because bcrypt salts make each incarnation unique.

parameters.name: UpgradePasswordHash
parameters.description:
UpgradePasswordHash raises the hash work factor after a successful login
without revoking otherwise-valid sessions. The exact-hash compare-and-set
prevents a slow bcrypt upgrade from overwriting a concurrent reset.

parameters.name: RecordFailedLogin
parameters.type: func(context.Context, schema.StableID, string, time.Time, int, time.Duration) (AuthCredential, error)

parameters.name: CreateSession
parameters.description:
CreateSession atomically verifies the exact password hash observed by
password authentication before persisting the new bearer session.

parameters.name: CreateAPIKey
parameters.description: CreateAPIKey inserts the key only while the authorizing session remains active. Password replacement serializes through the same credential row and cannot leave a late-created key behind.

parameters.name: AllowAuthAttempt
parameters.type: func(context.Context, string, time.Time, time.Duration, int) (bool, error)

details: Implementations must make failed-attempt updates and session rotation atomic across processes. Password hashes and token digests are private state and never enter document values, hooks, manifests, or protocol responses. AuthTransaction and AuthBootstrapTransaction bind credential creation to content transactions.

symbols.name: AuthMaintenanceStore
symbols.summary: Bounded pruning of expired auth state.
details: The implementation uses its authoritative clock, removes at most limit sessions and limit API keys, and must not double-count across concurrent callers. The batch is capped by MaxAuthPruneBatch (500).

parameters.name: Put
parameters.type: func(context.Context, string, io.Reader, int64, string) error

details: Put must atomically replace an existing key. Delete of a missing key must succeed. List returns a bounded, unique, key-ordered page under the requested prefix and every result has an authoritative non-zero ModifiedAt.
Ridu revalidates namespace ownership and committed upload references immediately before orphan cleanup. Return storage.ErrNotFound from Open when appropriate.

modules.name: migration
modules.summary: Advanced, database-independent vocabulary for immutable and reviewable migration artifacts.

symbols.name: Artifact
symbols.summary: The immutable definition of one migration.

parameters.name: Version
parameters.description: Version identifies this Ridu artifact JSON format.

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Name is the lowercase author-supplied migration name.

parameters.name: Planner
parameters.description: Planner records the exact planner and version used at creation.

parameters.name: MinimumRunnerContract
parameters.description:
MinimumRunnerContract is the lowest execution contract that may run
every phase and executor in this artifact.

parameters.name: PreviousArtifactDigest
parameters.description:
PreviousArtifactDigest binds this artifact to the exact preceding artifact,
including data-only transitions whose manifest digest does not change.
It is empty only for the initial artifact.

parameters.name: FromDigest
parameters.description: FromDigest and ToDigest establish immutable manifest lineage.

parameters.name: Before
parameters.description: Before is absent only for an initial migration from an empty schema.

parameters.name: After
parameters.description: After is the complete desired manifest after every step succeeds.

parameters.name: Phases
parameters.description: Phases are the resumable execution plan.

parameters.name: Risks
parameters.description: Risks retains machine-readable planner and linter findings for review.

details: ArtifactVersion is 1. Incompatible historical formats are intentionally unsupported. Application authors normally use ridu migrate commands and review the artifact rather than construct it by hand.

parameters.name: AllowInsecureTransport
parameters.description:
AllowInsecureTransport explicitly permits plaintext PostgreSQL connections.
Keep this false in production; it exists for local Unix sockets and
development databases whose transport is secured outside PostgreSQL.

parameters.name: MaxUploadLockConnections
parameters.description:
MaxUploadLockConnections bounds the separate advisory-lock pool used
while object storage and document transactions are coordinated. Keeping
this pool separate prevents staged uploads from starving their own
document transactions. Zero selects four connections.

details: Zero values select bounded Ridu defaults. Negative duration values explicitly disable the corresponding timeout.

AllowInsecureTransport is for local sockets or externally secured development transport; keep it false in production. The upload lock pool defaults to four connections and stays separate so staged uploads cannot starve their own document transactions.

symbols.summary: Explicit operational admissions, bounded timeouts, and resumable boundaries.

parameters.name: AllowInsecureDatabase
parameters.description:
AllowInsecureDatabase explicitly permits a PostgreSQL connection that can
fall back to plaintext. It is intended only for local migration drills.

parameters.name: AllowMaintenance
parameters.description:
AllowMaintenance admits traffic-sensitive semantic steps such as content
rewrites, compiled data transforms, resource retirement, and
reference-index rebuilds. Every old writer must be stopped while they run.
It does not relax artifact validation.

parameters.name: AllowUnbounded
parameters.description:
AllowUnbounded permits a zero operational timeout. Without this explicit
admission, zero selects the runner's bounded production default.

parameters.name: AdvisoryLockWait
parameters.description: AdvisoryLockWait bounds how long this runner waits for another migrator.

parameters.name: LockTimeout
parameters.description: LockTimeout bounds PostgreSQL lock acquisition inside a phase.

parameters.name: StatementTimeout
parameters.description: StatementTimeout bounds one transactional SQL statement.

parameters.name: BatchTimeout
parameters.description: BatchTimeout bounds the complete execution of one checkpoint batch.

parameters.name: ConcurrentIndexTimeout
parameters.description: ConcurrentIndexTimeout bounds one CREATE/DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY command.

parameters.name: IdleInTransactionTimeout
parameters.description: IdleInTransactionTimeout protects a paused transactional phase.

parameters.name: StopAfterPhase
parameters.description:
StopAfterPhase and StopAfterStep are explicit, successfully committed
rollout boundaries. A transaction phase can stop only at its final step.

parameters.name: Notice
parameters.description: Notice reports the migration runner identity after pending history passes preflight.

details: AllowMaintenance admits traffic-sensitive steps only after every old writer and worker is stopped; it does not relax artifact validation. Zero timeouts use bounded defaults unless AllowUnbounded is explicit.

symbols.name: Config
symbols.summary: Bounded connection behavior for the embedded SQLite store.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: Path is a filesystem path, a file: SQLite URI, or :memory:.

parameters.name: BusyTimeout
parameters.description:
BusyTimeout bounds how long SQLite waits for another writer. Zero selects
ten seconds. Negative values and values above SQLite's signed 32-bit
millisecond limit are rejected.

parameters.name: DisableWAL
parameters.description:
DisableWAL keeps file databases in their existing journal mode. WAL is
enabled by default because it permits readers while the single writer is
active. SQLite memory databases ignore WAL mode.

parameters.name: MaxConnections
parameters.description:
MaxConnections bounds pooled readers. Operation transactions still use
BEGIN IMMEDIATE and SQLite's single-writer contract.

details: Zero values select safe local defaults. File databases enable WAL unless DisableWAL is set; SQLite still has one writer.

modules.name: mongodb
modules.summary: The official replica-set MongoDB store, additive development index synchronization, and immutable forward-only migration lifecycle.

symbols.name: Open
symbols.summary: Open a verified-TLS MongoDB replica-set database with bounded defaults.
symbols.signature: func Open(ctx context.Context, databaseURL string) (*Store, error)
details: The URL must select one database. Open checks for a writable replica-set primary with logical sessions but does not create collections, indexes, or migration state.

symbols.name: OpenWithConfig
symbols.summary: Open the store with explicit transport, timeout, application-name, and pool bounds.
symbols.signature: func OpenWithConfig(ctx context.Context, config Config) (*Store, error)

symbols.name: Config
symbols.summary: Runtime-only MongoDB connection behavior.

parameters.name: DatabaseURL
parameters.description: Credential-bearing URL selecting the application database.

parameters.name: AllowInsecureTransport
parameters.description: Allow an insecure local development connection; keep false in production.

parameters.name: ApplicationName
parameters.description: Client application name; defaults to ridu.

parameters.name: ConnectTimeout
parameters.description: Connection bound; zero selects the Ridu default.

parameters.name: ServerSelectionTimeout
parameters.description: Primary-selection bound; zero selects the Ridu default.

parameters.name: MaxConnectionIdleTime
parameters.description: Pooled idle-time bound; zero selects the Ridu default.

parameters.name: MaxPoolSize
parameters.description: Maximum pool size; zero selects ten.

parameters.name: MinPoolSize
parameters.description: Minimum pool size; cannot exceed MaxPoolSize.

details: DatabaseURL never belongs in manifests, artifacts, generated contracts, or diagnostics. Negative durations and invalid pool bounds are rejected.

symbols.name: Store
symbols.summary: A replica-set implementation of Ridu’s document, snapshot, auth, preference, task, lock, upload, readiness, and migration contracts.
symbols.signature:
type Store struct {
	client   *mongo.Client
	database *mongo.Database
	now      func() time.Time

	closeMu  sync.Mutex
	closed   bool
	closeErr error

	indexLifecycleMu            sync.Mutex
	indexesMu                   sync.RWMutex
	verifiedIndexes             map[schema.StableID]mongoVerifiedIndexPlan
	verifiedVersionIndexes      map[schema.StableID]bool
	verifiedReferenceIndexes    bool
	verifiedPreferenceIndexes   bool
	verifiedDocumentLockIndexes bool
	verifiedTaskIndexes         bool
	verifiedAuthIndexes         bool
	verifiedUploadLockIndexes   bool

	uploadLockRetry time.Duration
	uploadLockWait  time.Duration

	uploadLockLifecycleMu     sync.Mutex
	uploadLockLifecycleCtx    context.Context
	uploadLockLifecycleCancel context.CancelFunc
	uploadLockOperations      sync.WaitGroup
}

parameters.name: store.MigrationReadinessStore
parameters.description: Checks the complete ledger against the release-binary fingerprint.

parameters.name: store.AuthStore
parameters.description: Persists credentials, sessions, tokens, API keys, and rate limits.

parameters.name: store.AuthMaintenanceStore
parameters.description: Prunes expired auth records in bounded batches.

parameters.name: store.UploadObjectLocker
parameters.description: Coordinates upload object changes across processes.

details: Use the application and Local API for content operations; the adapter exposes no raw BSON filter, database handle, ObjectID contract, or second Mongo-specific content API.
Transactions add auth/bootstrap/unlock, versions, distinct, windows, upload-reference lookup, and transaction-level upload locking to store.Transaction.

Production support is limited to generated starter and blank applications on Linux x86-64 with MongoDB Community 8.2.9, SCRAM-SHA-256, verified TLS, and a writable three-member replica set. Atlas, DocumentDB, Cosmos DB, standalone or sharded deployments, and other versions, topologies, and platforms are not supported.

details: It compares every ordered ledger filename and artifact digest with the ridu build fingerprint, verifies indexes without mutation, then rereads the ledger to reject a concurrent change.

symbols.name: CreateArtifact
symbols.summary: Publish an artifact with the frozen legacy MongoDB planner 1.0.0 creator.
symbols.signature: func CreateArtifact(ctx context.Context, directory, name string, after schema.Manifest, now time.Time) (CreatedArtifact, error)
details: This legacy-v1 entry point remains only for existing direct callers and immutable-history compatibility. New application and CLI-facing migrations use CreateArtifactWithOptions and planner 2.0.0.
Planning is offline and never receives a database URL, secret, or live MongoDB state.

symbols.name: CreateArtifactWithOptions
symbols.summary: Publish the current MongoDB planner 2.0.0 artifact with reviewed semantic intent.
symbols.signature: func CreateArtifactWithOptions(ctx context.Context, directory, name string, after schema.Manifest, now time.Time, options ArtifactOptions) (CreatedArtifact, error)
details: This is the creator used by ridu migrate create. It validates the immutable prefix, freezes confirmed renames and transform descriptors, records reviewed retirement/destructive findings, and never opens MongoDB.

symbols.name: InspectArtifacts
symbols.summary: Inspect exact local history against the live ledger without mutation.
symbols.signature: func InspectArtifacts(ctx context.Context, config Config, directory string, executableManifest schema.Manifest) ([]MigrationStatus, error)
details: CLI plan/status validates and precompiles the exact in-memory history through the executable manifest before connecting, then uses that retained snapshot for every ledger check.

symbols.name: VerifyArtifacts
symbols.summary: Replay complete immutable history through the adapter runner in an isolated shadow database.
symbols.signature: func VerifyArtifacts(ctx context.Context, config Config, directory string, transforms ...ridumigration.DataTransform) error
details: The operational credential creates and drops a randomly named shadow database; application collections are not used. Semantic histories use VerifyArtifactsWithOptions with explicit maintenance admission because verification replays the complete history.

symbols.name: VerifyArtifactsWithOptions
symbols.summary: Verify complete history with explicit maintenance admission and bounded runner controls.
symbols.signature: func VerifyArtifactsWithOptions(ctx context.Context, config Config, directory string, options RunnerOptions, transforms ...ridumigration.DataTransform) error

symbols.name: ProjectMigrations
symbols.summary: Build the compiled-project driver for checksum-bound transaction-scoped data transforms.
details: Callbacks remain compiled into the application; artifacts contain only validated names and checksums. MongoDB owns their transactions, checkpoints, and private connection boundary.

symbols.name: RunnerOptions
symbols.summary: Explicit maintenance admission and bounded lease/operation controls.
symbols.signature:
type RunnerOptions struct {
	AllowMaintenance bool
	AllowUnbounded   bool
	LeaseWait        time.Duration
	LeaseDuration    time.Duration
	OperationTimeout time.Duration
}

parameters.name: AllowMaintenance
parameters.description: Admit pending traffic-sensitive live steps after writers drain, or complete semantic shadow replay.

parameters.name: AllowUnbounded
parameters.description: Explicitly permit a zero wait or operation timeout.

parameters.name: LeaseWait
parameters.description: Maximum wait for the single-migrator fenced lease.

parameters.name: LeaseDuration
parameters.description: Renewable bounded lease duration used for crash recovery.

details: Zero values select bounded defaults unless AllowUnbounded explicitly admits an unbounded wait or operation; lease expiry remains bounded.

details: Only an absolute path on the configured Ridu origin is accepted; network paths, full URLs, and fragments are rejected before dispatch.
The raw Response is returned for every HTTP status. No JSON content type is added implicitly, so the caller retains complete request and response control.
The request still uses configured credentials, merged headers, middleware, abort signals, and keepalive behavior.

parameters.name: directory
parameters.description: New project directory, which must not already exist.

details: The scaffold is kept if dependency setup or initial generation fails, and the CLI prints recovery commands.
--release-version is a framework-development override for exercising an alternate dependency release; ordinary application authors should not use it.
symbols.example:
ridu new --package-manager npm \
	--module github.com/acme/content \
	--scope @acme \
	content
cd content
npm install
npm run dev

symbols.name: ridu agent install
symbols.summary: Install a release-matched local agent layout into an existing Ridu project.
details: Installs both ridu-project and payload-to-ridu with their offline references. Existing AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md instructions are preserved, and unmanaged skill files are never replaced.
.ridu-agent-docs.json records only framework-owned files, digests, selected layouts, and the framework release.
symbols.example: ridu agent install --agent claude

symbols.name: ridu agent sync
symbols.summary: Synchronize installed framework-owned skill references with the current CLI release.
details: Sync validates every recorded digest before writing and stops if a managed file contains local edits. Root project instructions are never synchronized.

symbols.name: ridu doctor
symbols.summary: Diagnose Go, Bun, project discovery, frontend dependencies, and local database prerequisites.
details: Docker or OrbStack is optional when DATABASE_URL is already set for PostgreSQL or MongoDB, and is not required for SQLite projects. doctor validates RIDU_SQLITE_PATH when configured and reports whether frontend dependencies are installed or will be installed by dev/build.

symbols.name: ridu dev
symbols.summary: Run the selected database adapter, generation, safe schema sync, API, admin watch mode, and Go-config watching together.

parameters.name: --database-url
parameters.description: PostgreSQL or MongoDB development URL; defaults to DATABASE_URL, then the selected scaffold Compose service.

parameters.name: --database-path
parameters.description: SQLite-only development path; defaults to RIDU_SQLITE_PATH, then .ridu/development.sqlite.

parameters.name: --address
parameters.description: Go API listen address; defaults to 127.0.0.1:8080.

parameters.name: --no-docker
parameters.description: Do not start the scaffolded PostgreSQL or MongoDB Compose service.

parameters.name: --no-install
parameters.description: Do not install missing frontend dependencies with the configured package manager.

parameters.name: --no-sync
parameters.description: Do not apply a safe non-destructive development schema plan.

details: Automatic sync pauses instead of guessing when a possible rename needs review. Create and apply a migration, then restart dev.
Development injects local-only insecure cookie/database admissions into the child server; those are not production defaults.
symbols.example:
ridu dev --database-url "$DATABASE_URL" --no-docker
ridu dev --database-path .ridu/development.sqlite

symbols.name: ridu generate
symbols.summary: Resolve executable Go config and atomically write every configured generated contract.

parameters.name: --check
parameters.description: Compare expected bytes without writing; exit unsuccessfully on missing or stale output.

details: Generation executes the application’s versioned private manifest command; it never parses Go source and never connects to the database.
Configured outputs include the canonical schema manifest, Go and TypeScript contracts/client module, OpenAPI, and static admin plugin registry.
symbols.example:
ridu generate
git diff -- generated/
ridu generate --check

symbols.name: ridu check
symbols.summary: Run the generated-contract, migration-history, Go, TypeScript, and Svelte project checks.
details: The command checks generation drift, current migration history, gofmt, go vet, go test ./..., then the project Bun check script when an admin is configured. It does not silently regenerate stale contracts.

symbols.name: ridu build
symbols.summary: Regenerate contracts, build the admin, and atomically install one production Go binary.

parameters.name: --output
parameters.description: Binary path; defaults to dist/<project> (with .exe on Windows).

details: Missing frontend dependencies are installed first. The admin assets are compiled before go build -trimpath; the final binary is renamed into place only after a successful build.
symbols.example: ridu build --output ./bin/content

symbols.name: ridu migrate create
symbols.summary: Plan and write one reviewable immutable migration artifact without connecting to a database.

parameters.name: --accept-renames
parameters.description: PostgreSQL or MongoDB: accept every unambiguous detected rename without an interactive prompt.

parameters.name: --transform
parameters.description: SQLite or MongoDB: bind a named compiled data transform to the immutable artifact.

parameters.name: --allow-destructive
parameters.description: Record destructive changes confirmed by the selected adapter planner after explicit review.

details: PostgreSQL and MongoDB rename candidates require confirmation or --accept-renames. SQLite rejects --accept-renames and uses --transform instead for stored canonical JSON rewrites. MongoDB transforms run through the compiled project migration driver. Destructive approval does not bypass semantic transitions Ridu cannot safely automate.
symbols.example:
ridu migrate create --name rename-post-title
git diff -- migrations/

symbols.name: ridu migrate plan
symbols.summary: Inspect pending immutable execution topology without applying it.
details: PostgreSQL and MongoDB use --database-url or DATABASE_URL and accept --allow-insecure-database only for local development; SQLite uses --database-path or RIDU_SQLITE_PATH. Current executable config must match the latest artifact target before database inspection proceeds. JSON output exposes adapter-owned phase, step, checksum, and state details.

symbols.name: ridu migrate status
symbols.summary: Compare immutable artifact history with the database ledger.
details: PostgreSQL and MongoDB use --database-url or DATABASE_URL; SQLite uses --database-path or RIDU_SQLITE_PATH. Status is read-only and does not accept maintenance, timeout, or stop-boundary flags. MongoDB status validates immutable lineage, checksum-bound durable progress, and exact physical state.

symbols.name: ridu migrate verify
symbols.summary: Replay complete history in an isolated adapter-owned database and validate every intermediate state.
details: PostgreSQL verification uses a temporary shadow schema and accepts runner timeout controls but not stop boundaries. SQLite needs no deployment path and replays history, including registered compiled transforms, in a temporary database. MongoDB uses a command-scoped credential to create, replay, verify, and drop a random shadow database; use separate scoped credentials for the running application, verification, and backups.

symbols.name: ridu migrate up
symbols.summary: Validate complete history and apply pending artifacts under adapter-owned coordination.
details: PostgreSQL requires secure transport unless explicitly admitted, holds a session advisory lock, and resumes durable phased checkpoints. SQLite applies every pending artifact atomically under one BEGIN IMMEDIATE writer reservation. MongoDB requires verified TLS unless explicitly admitted for local development, holds a fenced expiring lease, and resumes checksum-bound durable steps.
symbols.example:
DATABASE_URL="$MONGODB_MIGRATION_URL" ridu migrate plan --json
# Drain every old application process, worker, and other writer.
DATABASE_URL="$MONGODB_OPERATIONAL_URL" ridu migrate verify
# Capture the matched database/upload snapshot.
DATABASE_URL="$MONGODB_MIGRATION_URL" ridu migrate up
DATABASE_URL="$MONGODB_MIGRATION_URL" ridu migrate status
# Start only the new digest; require /readyz before admitting traffic.
DATABASE_URL="$MONGODB_APP_URL" ./dist/content

symbols.name: ridu migrate down
symbols.summary: Reverse the latest applied SQLite artifact while retaining its immutable file.
details: SQLite only. The path may instead come from RIDU_SQLITE_PATH. Status reports the reversed artifact as pending so migrate up can replay it.

symbols.name: ridu migrate reset
symbols.summary: Reverse every applied SQLite artifact in exact reverse order.
details: SQLite only. The path may instead come from RIDU_SQLITE_PATH. Artifact files and checksums remain committed; schema, callbacks, and ledger changes roll back atomically.

symbols.name: ridu migrate refresh
symbols.summary: Reverse and replay complete committed SQLite history atomically.
details: SQLite only. The path may instead come from RIDU_SQLITE_PATH. Registered compiled down and up callbacks run with their checksum-bound artifacts in the same transaction.

symbols.name: ridu migrate fresh
symbols.summary: Drop non-internal SQLite objects and replay committed history atomically.
details: SQLite only. The path may instead come from RIDU_SQLITE_PATH. Use this explicit destructive workflow for a reviewed local rebuild, not as production startup synchronization.

symbols.name: PostgreSQL migration runner options
symbols.summary: PostgreSQL operational admissions and bounds accepted by migrate up and, except stop boundaries, verify.
details: --allow-maintenance requires every application process and worker to remain stopped through completion and retries.
Zero durations select bounded defaults unless --allow-unbounded is explicit.
--stop-after-phase and --stop-after-step are accepted only by PostgreSQL migrate up; verify always runs to completion.

symbols.name: MongoDB migration runner options
symbols.summary: MongoDB operational admissions and bounds accepted by migrate up and verify.
details: --allow-maintenance requires every application process and worker to remain stopped through completion and retries.

--advisory-lock-wait bounds acquisition of the fenced migration lease; --concurrent-index-timeout bounds the complete MongoDB migration operation. Zero selects bounded defaults unless --allow-unbounded is explicit, and lease expiry remains bounded.

MongoDB rejects the PostgreSQL-only --lock-timeout, --statement-timeout, --batch-timeout, --idle-in-transaction-timeout, --stop-after-phase, and --stop-after-step controls. Interrupted work resumes from the checksum-bound durable step ledger.

symbols.name: ridu plugin new
symbols.summary: Scaffold paired Go and Svelte plugin packages with conformance tests.
details: The key must be stable and lowercase. Publish the Go and admin packages with matching plugin pairing versions after both conformance suites pass.
symbols.example:
ridu plugin new ./ridu-color \
	--key color \
	--module example.com/acme/ridu-color \
	--admin-package @acme/ridu-color-admin

symbols.name: ridu plugin add
symbols.summary: Install and register a compiled backend plugin and optional paired admin package.

parameters.name: --go-version
parameters.description: Go module requirement; defaults to latest.

parameters.name: --constructor
parameters.description: Exported zero-argument constructor; defaults to New.

parameters.name: --admin-version
parameters.description: Admin package requirement; defaults to latest.

parameters.name: --no-install
parameters.description: Update registration without invoking Go or the configured frontend package manager.

details: ridu add is an exact alias. The command updates dependencies and registration, regenerates contracts, checks compatibility, and rolls back its files on failure. Review the descriptor and create a migration afterward.

symbols.name: ridu plugin remove
symbols.summary: Remove static plugin registration and dependencies, then regenerate contracts.
details: Without --no-install the command removes the Bun dependency and runs go mod tidy. It rolls back on generation failure. Create a migration to review any plugin down steps.

symbols.name: ridu version
symbols.summary: Print the compiled CLI version.

symbols.name: ridu help
symbols.summary: Show commands and the compiled project-protocol and schema-manifest versions.
